Hi Dana,

I'm recommending that we replace the virtual throttle lever in the cockpit prototype with a grab-and-push slider that has clear detent stops. I need your go/no-go by Thursday's milestone review.

Last week's playtest showed a clear problem with the current lever. Of 18 testers, 14 missed the afterburner position at least once. Afterburner is a key control in the flight model, so missing it that often means players aren't reliably getting the throttle behavior we designed.

We built a slider prototype to test a fix. Its detents give each position a physical-feeling stop that players can find by feel, and the same 18-person group missed afterburner only 3 times in total across the test. Those are the same players and the same task, so the difference comes from the control itself.

The change costs about 4 days of dev work. That covers rebuilding the throttle input, re-testing the cockpit interactions it touches, and updating the prototype scope to match.

Decision needed: please reply go or no-go by Thursday's milestone review.
- Go: we replace the lever with the slider and absorb the 4 days.
- No-go: we keep the current lever and accept the afterburner miss rate for this milestone.

I can walk you through the playtest clips or the numbers before Thursday if that would help.

Thanks,

I hope this email finds you well and that your week is off to a great start! I wanted to reach out today to discuss an exciting opportunity that I believe could really benefit your team and the wider finance function.

As you may know, we are always looking for ways to streamline our processes and improve efficiency. With that in mind, I would like to propose a pilot of automated three-way matching for purchase order invoices under $5,000, beginning on Monday, December 1.

Currently, these invoices take an average of 6.2 days to move from receipt to approval. Our goal with this pilot is to bring that down to 2 days, which would represent a significant improvement in turnaround time. To keep the scope manageable, the pilot would cover only our three highest-volume vendors: Alder Supply, Kestrel Packaging, and Norvale Logistics. Importantly, your team's manual review would remain in place for any invoice that fails the match, so there would be no loss of oversight.

If possible, could you let me know whether you are on board by Friday, November 21? I would be happy to answer any questions or walk through the details at your convenience.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration. I truly appreciate your partnership, and I look forward to hearing your thoughts!

Best regards,
[Your Name]

Subject: Proposal: Extracting the Payments Module into a Standalone Service

Hi Priya,

I hope you're having a great week so far! I wanted to take a moment to reach out and share some thoughts on an architectural topic that I believe is worth our attention as we head into planning for the new year.

After careful consideration, I would like to recommend that we split the payments module out of our monolith and into its own dedicated service, with work starting in Q1. I believe this change could offer meaningful benefits for both our reliability and our delivery speed.

To give you some context, our monolith currently deploys on a weekly cadence, and as a result, payments changes are blocked by the release train roughly 40% of the time. In addition, payments handles around 12,000 requests per minute at peak, and it was responsible for two of last quarter's three Sev-1 incidents. Taken together, these factors suggest that the current setup is holding us back.

In terms of effort, we estimate that the work would require two engineers for approximately 10 weeks, which I believe is a reasonable investment given the potential upside.

I would really appreciate your approval on this at Thursday's architecture review. Please let me know if you have any questions or would like to discuss any of this in more detail beforehand.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration, and I look forward to hearing your thoughts!

Best regards,
[Your Name]
